name: Audio fingerprint (OfflineAudioContext)
plain: Renders a sound offline and reads tiny numeric differences.
meaning: Audio stack differences give a device specific value without ever playing sound or asking permission. LinkedIn uses OfflineAudioContext(1,44100,44100).

limits.headline: Can make a silent test sound to tell your device apart from others
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads
can: Process a short sound in memory without playing it
Measure tiny number differences that depend on your device and browser
Combine that number with other signals to recognise you later
cannot: Ask you first, since there is no pop up
Work as an ID on its own, because many similar devices give the same result

story.what_it_is: A page plays a sound silently in memory and reads tiny number differences that vary by device.

marketing.name: OfflineAudioContext
marketing.pitch: Renders audio faster than real time into a buffer, without playing it to the speakers, for effects and analysis.

story.for_you: You hear nothing and see no prompt. The page just does some math that a sound chip would do, and the answer helps it recognize your device later.
story.for_makers: Trackers and fraud teams add this to a bundle of signals to build a device ID. It is cheap, needs no permission, and is hard for people to notice. The real feature exists so audio apps can process sound offline.

use_cases.example: A web music studio renders a finished track to a file offline, much faster than playing it back.
A browser game builds echo or reverb effects ahead of time so sound effects play instantly in battle.
A bank's fraud script plays a silent tone and compares the result with the last visit to confirm it is the same device.
An ad tech script adds the audio result to a device ID to recognize you across sites without cookies.
A visitor counting tool uses the audio hash to avoid double counting the same person who cleared cookies.
A podcast editor in the browser exports a mixed episode by rendering all tracks offline.
A page prepares sound effects for screen reader users before they hear them.

risks: Browsers are adding noise to fight it

technical_bounds: Noise added by some privacy browsers
